A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same STaRFormer research and contain readable text, equations, figures and tables supporting reliable comparison. V2 ends with references and contains no appendix; v3 includes substantial supplementary material in Appendices A-D.

before.justification: V2 reports original STaRFormer classification results on 15 datasets, component ablations, parameter sensitivity studies and latent-space visualizations in Section 4.

after.justification: V3 retains original classification experiments and adds healthcare classification, anomaly detection, regression and noise-robustness results, with detailed experimental records in Appendix D.

M1.justification: The shared Transformer backbone, DAReM and sequence-level classification losses remain. V3 adds element-level contrastive losses with within-sequence and between-sequence pairing, regression supervision through k-means target pseudo-labels, and corresponding prediction heads. It also incorporates RoBERTa-encoded static attributes for healthcare datasets. These are substantive procedural adaptations.

E1.justification: Coverage expands from 15 classification datasets to 56 datasets. V3 retains the original coverage and adds P19/P12 healthcare classification, 18 additional UEA datasets, Yahoo/KPI anomaly detection and 19 TSR regression datasets (Table 8). It also evaluates controlled noise-corruption scenarios on DKT.

E2.justification: V3 adds TARNet and TimesURL to DKT/GL comparisons, DGM2-O and MTGNN to PAM, and WEASEL-MUSE and several contrastive methods to UEA. The GL comparison removes Time-LSTM, Random Forest and CNN. New anomaly-detection and regression experiments introduce additional comparator sets (Tables 1-5, 30 and 33).

E3.justification: New protocols include healthcare AUROC/AUPRC evaluation, chronological half-training/half-testing anomaly detection with windowed inputs, and regression RMSE aggregation. UEA summaries change from the common eight-dataset comparison to 30-, 28- and nine-dataset comparisons. V3 also introduces the DKT corruption protocol. GL masking settings conflict between v3 Tables 7 and 24, leaving that specific setting change unresolved.

E4.justification: V3 adds a Gaussian-noise robustness analysis on long DKT sequences (Table 14) and trained-versus-untrained PAM similarity heatmaps (Figure 11). Architecture ablations expand from 15 to 19 datasets. Existing contrastive-component removals, loss-weight and masking-region sweeps, and t-SNE analyses are retained, with some revised results and relocated displays.

E5.justification: V2 already reports five-seed or five-split experiments with means and standard deviations. V3 specifies seed identities, adds medians and detailed run records, and clarifies single-seed benchmark reporting in Appendix D.3. This refines statistical disclosure without establishing increased replication or introducing inferential significance tests.

E6.justification: V3 adds extensive results, including Yahoo/KPI F1 scores of 0.789/0.830 and the TSR regression results. Retained DKT baseline accuracies change from 0.847 to 0.844 for LSTM and 0.849 to 0.840 for GRU, while STaRFormer remains at 0.852. V3 Table 31 corrects the swapped EW/EC ablation entries in v2 Table 5. Some PAM ablation metrics disagree between v3 Tables 7 and 27.

T1.justification: V3 adds formal anomaly-detection and regression problems and substantial element-level contrastive definitions, including pair-selection masks (Equations 3-5 and 41-43). The original classification and rollout equations are retained. The new sequence-indicator expression preceding Equation 4 evaluates to zero throughout its stated index range, creating a mathematical inconsistency. No performance theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The central claims remain that DAReM combined with batch-wise/class-wise contrastive learning improves task-specific representations and downstream predictions across diverse time-series types. Both versions already present STaRFormer as a universal framework. The additional datasets and tasks primarily provide broader support for this existing claim.

C2.justification: V3 adds limitations concerning task-specific retraining and distinguishes training overhead from inference cost. Appendix D.2 attributes limited DKT accuracy gains to overlapping labels and an approximately 90% performance ceiling, then interprets noise sensitivity. Appendix D.3.9 acknowledges that accuracy is unsuitable for some imbalanced and anomaly-detection datasets. These substantially expand v2's mainly computational limitation discussion.

D1.justification: V3 adds masking pseudocode, output-head specifications, masking search ranges, preprocessing and split descriptions, optimizer/scheduler information, and detailed runtime, memory and hardware records. It supplies repository and configuration-access instructions. V2's general future code/data-release promise is replaced by more specific access information and explicit restrictions preventing release of DKT data and associated code.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially expands positioning against task-agnostic contrastive approaches, adding discussion of TS2Vec, CoST, InfoTS and TimesURL. It explicitly presents DAReM as a generalization of TARNet's masking and contrasts joint task-specific learning with reusable universal representations. The appendix also expands methodological background and task-specific references.

P1.justification: V3 substantially rewrites and reorders the introduction and related-work narrative, reorganizes the method around three task formulations, and regroups experiments by task. Existing explanations move into structured appendices, the contrastive and regional-masking discussions are combined, and extensive explanatory background, a glossary and a checklist are added.

P2.justification: V3 merges the DKT/GL result displays and the contrastive/masking ablation tables, introduces benchmark summaries with detailed appendix tables, and adds data illustrations, similarity heatmaps and compute/run tables. The architecture diagram is reannotated. V2 Figure 2 is split into v3 Figures 8-9, while the existing t-SNE display becomes Figure 2.

improvement.justification: V2's broad generality and robustness claims had classification-only validation and sparse implementation disclosure. V3's explicit task adaptations, expanded comparisons, direct noise analysis and detailed preprocessing/run/compute documentation substantially reduce those validation and reproducibility gaps. The new indexing inconsistency near Equation 4 and disagreements such as Tables 7/27 weaken parts of the added material, and DKT remains non-public. Nevertheless, the gains in experimental scrutiny, documented limitations and transparency outweigh these defects.
